# Eject widens the opt-in: the fork enables extended CONNECT per server
# while stock Go offers only the process-global GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1.
# The rewritten call delegates to the ejected support module, which
# requires that setting in the process startup environment and panics
# naming the server otherwise, so ejected servers fail fast instead of
# serving without it.

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

cd m
logos run .
stdout '^h2 extended connect ready$'
stdout '^deferred registered: true$'
stdout '^async registered: true$'
cp stdout $WORK/native.txt
logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
! grep 'EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect' out/main.go
grep 'RequireExtendedConnect' out/main.go
grep 'http2xconnect=1' out/_logos_deps/rt/logos/net/http/h2extendedconnect_ejected.go
grep 'ejectedhttp "github.com/gosuda/loGos/rt/logos/net/http"' out/main.go
! grep 'os.Getenv' out/main.go
! grep 'strings.Contains' out/main.go
grep 'func RequireExtendedConnect' out/_logos_deps/rt/logos/net/http/h2extendedconnect_ejected.go
cd out
go build ./...
env GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1
go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt
env GODEBUG=
! exec go run .
stderr 'needs GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1'
stderr 'on server "srv"'
env GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1
exec go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt
exists $UPROOT1272/bin/go
exec $UPROOT1272/bin/go version
stdout '^go version go1\.27\.2 '
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
cd ..

# A receiver that carries error-tracing temporaries from '?' inside an
# inline callback cannot be rewritten without overlapping the tracing
# edits, so eject leaves it alone. Verification must refuse it instead of
# passing a fork-only method into output upstream Go rejects.
cd ../trace
logos run .
stdout '^trace receiver stays native$'
! logos eject -o out
stderr 'fork_stdlib_api'
cd ..

# A user type with the same method name keeps its own binding: the method
# value in a net/http file is not lowering output, so the rewrite leaves
# it alone and the ejected program builds and runs with upstream Go.
cd uservalue
logos run .
stdout '^before defer: 0$'
stdout '^after defer: 1$'
cp stdout $WORK/usernative.txt
logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
grep 'f := m.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect' out/main.go
! grep 'RequireExtendedConnect' out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/usernative.txt
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/usernative.txt
cd ../..

# A direct call of the same name on a user type is ambiguous with the
# stdlib opt-in: the text rewrite matches by spelling, so verification
# refuses it instead of ejecting the wrong behavior.
cd usercall
logos build ./...
! logos eject -o out
stderr 'fork_stdlib_api.*ambiguous.*EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect'
! exists out
cd ..
# A grouped opt-in whose receiver holds another opt-in is refused at
# eject check: a call nested in another call's receiver span would lower
# into a site temporary overlapping the rewrite, so verification fails
# closed instead of emitting overlapping edits.
cd nested
logos run .
stdout '^nested ready$'
! logos eject -o out
stderr 'fork_stdlib_api'
cd ..

# A same-named user method that takes arguments ejects untouched: the
# opt-in takes no arguments, the direct rewrite needs zero arguments,
# and a lowered capture used with arguments keeps its binding, so an
# argument-bearing call can never be the genuine call and keeps its own
# behavior in the export, which upstream Go builds.
cd withargs
logos run .
stdout '^withargs ready$'
logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
grep 'm.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect' out/main.go
! grep 'RequireExtendedConnect' out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
stdout '^withargs ready$'
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go run .
stdout '^withargs ready$'
cd ../..

# A sibling file declaring the fresh alias at package level does not
# break the export: the support import alias avoids every package-level
# name in the ejected package, and upstream Go builds the result.
cd sibling
logos run .
stdout '^sibling ready$'
logos eject -o out
grep 'ejectedhttp2.RequireExtendedConnect' out/server.go
grep 'ejectedhttp2 "github.com/gosuda/loGos/rt/logos/net/http"' out/server.go
cd out
go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
env GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1
go run .
stdout '^sibling ready$'
cd ../..

# A plain Go file binding the fork-only method value is refused before
# writing: the rewrite leaves method values intact, so without the typed
# check the fork-only binding would reach upstream Go, which rejects it.
cd gofile
logos build ./...
! logos eject -o out
stderr 'fork_stdlib_api'
! exists out
cd ..

# A plain Go file binding a same-named user method value still ejects:
# the typed check tells it apart from the fork-only method.
cd gouser
logos build ./...
logos eject -o out
cd out
go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go run .
stdout '^gouser ready: 1$'
cd ../..

# A plain Go direct call with arguments ejects untouched: a file without
# net/http never reaches the rewrite, and the typed check tells the user
# method apart from the fork-only opt-in.
cd gouserargs
logos build ./...
logos eject -o out
grep 'm.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect\(2\)' out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
stdout '^gouserargs ready: 2$'
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go run .
stdout '^gouserargs ready: 2$'
cd ../..

# A server capture through a local that shadows the support import alias
# is still the server method: the verifier approves it by type, so the
# rewrite rebinds it through a fresh alias instead of skipping it by
# spelling, while the saved helper value in the same file keeps working.
cd shadowserver
logos run .
stdout '^helper used$'
stdout '^shadow server ready$'
logos eject -o out
grep 'ejectedhttp.RequireExtendedConnectFunc\("logohttp", logohttp\)' out/main.go
grep ':= logohttp.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect' out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
env GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1
go run .
stdout '^helper used$'
stdout '^shadow server ready$'
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
env GODEBUG=
cd ../..

# The ejected server really speaks extended CONNECT on the wire: with
# the process-global setting in effect, the native and the
# upstream-built binaries both advertise
# SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL, so the handshake pins what the
# ejected guard predicts.
cd h2wire
logos run .
stdout '^extended connect advertised$'
logos eject -o out
cd out
go build ./...
env GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1
go run .
stdout '^extended connect advertised$'
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go run .
stdout '^extended connect advertised$'
env GODEBUG=
cd ../..

# Saving the public logos/net/http helper as a value is not a lowered
# server method value: the rewrite leaves it alone, the import still
# remaps to the ejected support copy, and both binaries run it.
cd helper
logos run .
stdout '^helper ready$'
logos eject -o out
! grep 'RequireExtendedConnectFunc' out/main.go
grep 'logohttp.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect' out/main.go
grep 'logohttp "github.com/gosuda/loGos/rt/logos/net/http"' out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
env GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1
go run .
stdout '^helper ready$'
env GODEBUG=
! exec go run .
stderr 'needs GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1'
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
cd ../..

# A user method declared in the same file as its call needs no rewrite:
# the emitter skips files declaring the name, so ejection keeps the method
# and the call unchanged, including through a nested receiver that returns
# the user type, and upstream Go builds them.
cd samefile
logos run .
stdout '^samefile meter: 1 4$'
logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
grep 'm.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()' out/main.go
! grep 'RequireExtendedConnect' out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
stdout '^samefile meter: 1 4$'
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go run .
stdout '^samefile meter: 1 4$'
cd ../..

# An optional call desugared by lowering is verified after lowering: the
# source `?.` records no selector, but the lowered ordinary call on
# *http.Server in a file without net/http has no rewrite and must be
# refused instead of reaching output upstream Go rejects.
cd optalias
logos run .
stdout '^optalias ready$'
! logos eject -o out
stderr 'fork_stdlib_api'
! exists out
cd ..

# A comptime instance calling a user method in a package without net/http
# keeps the call: no destination file can reach the rewrite, so there is
# nothing to refuse.
cd ctuser
logos run .
stdout '^ctuser meter: 1$'
logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
grep 'm.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()' out/main.go
! grep 'RequireExtendedConnect' out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
stdout '^ctuser meter: 1$'
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build ./...
cd ../..

# A module whose only net/http import and extended-CONNECT call live in
# a non-host variant still needs the helper package in the output: the
# variant inventory carries no import edges, so the seed-based roots miss
# logos/net/http and the support bundle is selected from the imports the
# rewrite actually emitted instead. The native run prints the host
# variant's message, so each host asserts its own.
cd variant
[!GOOS:windows] logos run .
[!GOOS:windows] stdout '^other ready$'
[GOOS:windows] logos run .
[GOOS:windows] stdout '^windows ready$'
logos eject -o out
grep 'RequireExtendedConnect' out/server_windows.go
grep 'ejectedhttp "github.com/gosuda/loGos/rt/logos/net/http"' out/server_windows.go
env GOOS=windows
env CGO_ENABLED=0
cd out
go build ./...
cd ../..

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/h2xconnect

go 1.27

-- m/main.lgo --

// Command h2xconnectdemo exercises eject of the extended-connect opt-in.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/tls"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	sys "os"
)

var registry = map[string]*http.Server{}

var mode = sys.Getenv("H2XCONNECT_MODE")

func getOrCreate(name string) *http.Server {
	if s, ok := registry[name]; ok {
		return s
	}
	s := &http.Server{
		Addr:      "127.0.0.1:0",
		TLSConfig: &tls.Config{MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13},
		Handler:   http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {}),
	}
	registry[name] = s
	return s
}

func run() error {
	srv := &http.Server{
		Addr:      "127.0.0.1:0",
		TLSConfig: &tls.Config{MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13},
		Handler:   http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {}),
	}
	srv.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	app{Server: srv}.start()
	strings := "shadow"
	_ = strings
	_ = mode
	defer getOrCreate("deferred").EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	go group (context.Background()) {
		go getOrCreate("async").EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	}
	fmt.Println("h2 extended connect ready")
	fmt.Println("deferred registered:", registry["deferred"] != nil)
	fmt.Println("async registered:", registry["async"] != nil)
	return nil
}

// app exercises the promoted opt-in: the call records the outer struct
// as its receiver, but the method object is the Server method the
// textual rewrite accepts.
type app struct{ *http.Server }

func (a app) start() {
	a.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
}

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}

-- trace/go.mod --
module example.com/h2trace

go 1.27

-- trace/main.lgo --

// Command h2tracedemo covers the unrewritable receiver: '?' inside the
// inline callback leaves tracing temporaries in the receiver subtree.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
)

func loadConfig() (string, error) {
	return "cfg", nil
}

func makeServer(init func() error) *http.Server {
	if err := init(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	return &http.Server{Addr: "127.0.0.1:0"}
}

func main() {
	makeServer(func() error { loadConfig()?; return nil }).EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	fmt.Println("trace receiver stays native")
}

package main

// Meter is a user type with the same opt-in name as the fork-only
// (*net/http.Server) method. Its method value must survive ejection.
type Meter struct{ Hits int }

func (m *Meter) EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect() { m.Hits++ }

-- uservalue/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
)

func main() {
	m := &Meter{}
	func() {
		f := m.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect
		defer f()
		fmt.Println("before defer:", m.Hits)
	}()
	fmt.Println("after defer:", m.Hits)
	srv := &http.Server{Addr: "127.0.0.1:0"}
	_ = srv
}

-- nested/go.mod --
module example.com/h2nested

go 1.27

-- nested/main.lgo --

// Command nesteddemo covers a grouped opt-in whose receiver holds another
// opt-in: eject composes the inner guard into the capture instead of
// emitting overlapping edits that stop the export.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
)

var backup = &http.Server{Addr: "127.0.0.1:0"}

func makeServer(init func()) *http.Server {
	init()
	return &http.Server{Addr: "127.0.0.1:0"}
}

func run() error {
	go group (context.Background()) {
		go makeServer(func() { backup.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect() }).EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	}
	fmt.Println("nested ready")
	return nil
}

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}

}

package main

import "fmt"

// Meter is a user type with the same opt-in name as the fork-only
// (*net/http.Server) method. A direct call with arguments can never be
// the zero-argument opt-in, so it ejects untouched.
type Meter struct{ Hits int }

func (m *Meter) EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect(level int) { m.Hits += level }

func main() {
	m := &Meter{}
	m.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect(2)
	fmt.Println("gouserargs ready:", m.Hits)
}

-- h2wire/go.mod --
module example.com/h2wire

go 1.27

-- h2wire/main.lgo --

// Command h2wiredemo serves with the opt-in and checks on the wire that
// the server advertises SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL. The client
// parses the SETTINGS frame by hand so the fixture needs only the
// standard library.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/ecdsa"
	"crypto/elliptic"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/tls"
	"crypto/x509"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"math/big"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"time"
)

func serveQuiet(srv *http.Server, ln net.Listener) {
	if err := srv.Serve(ln); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
		panic(err)
	}
}

func closeConn(conn *tls.Conn, err error) error {
	if cerr := conn.Close(); cerr != nil {
		return cerr
	}
	return err
}


func clientPreface() []byte {
	out := []byte("PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n")
	return append(out, 0, 0, 0, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
}

func settingsHasExtendedConnect(conn *tls.Conn) (bool, error) {
	if err := conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	var hdr [9]byte
	for {
		if _, err := io.ReadFull(conn, hdr[:]); err != nil {
			return false, err
		}
		length := int(hdr[0])<<16 | int(hdr[1])<<8 | int(hdr[2])
		typ := hdr[3]
		payload := make([]byte, length)
		if _, err := io.ReadFull(conn, payload); err != nil {
			return false, err
		}
		if typ != 4 {
			continue
		}
		for i := 0; i+6 <= len(payload); i += 6 {
			id := int(payload[i])<<8 | int(payload[i+1])
			if id == 8 {
				return true, nil
			}
		}
		return false, nil
	}
}

func handshake(addr string) error {
	conn, err := tls.Dial("tcp", addr, &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true, NextProtos: []string{"h2"}})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if proto := conn.ConnectionState().NegotiatedProtocol; proto != "h2" {
		return closeConn(conn, fmt.Errorf("h2wire: negotiated %q, want h2", proto))
	}
	if _, err := conn.Write(clientPreface()); err != nil {
		return closeConn(conn, err)
	}
	found, serr := settingsHasExtendedConnect(conn)
	cerr := conn.Close()
	if serr != nil {
		return serr
	}
	if cerr != nil {
		return cerr
	}
	if !found {
		return fmt.Errorf("h2wire: SETTINGS without ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL")
	}
	fmt.Println("extended connect advertised")
	return nil
}

func handshakeAndClose(addr string, srv *http.Server) error {
	herr := handshake(addr)
	if cerr := srv.Close(); cerr != nil && herr == nil {
		return cerr
	}
	return herr
}

func run() error {
	key, err := ecdsa.GenerateKey(elliptic.P256(), rand.Reader)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	tmpl := &x509.Certificate{SerialNumber: big.NewInt(1), NotBefore: time.Now().Add(-time.Hour), NotAfter: time.Now().Add(time.Hour)}
	tmpl.DNSNames = []string{"localhost"}
	tmpl.IPAddresses = []net.IP{net.ParseIP("127.0.0.1")}
	der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, tmpl, tmpl, &key.PublicKey, key)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	srv := &http.Server{
		Addr:      "127.0.0.1:0",
		TLSConfig: &tls.Config{Certificates: []tls.Certificate{{Certificate: [][]byte{der}, PrivateKey: key}}, NextProtos: []string{"h2"}},
		Handler:   http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {}),
	}
	srv.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	ln, err := tls.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0", srv.TLSConfig)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	go group (context.Background()) {
		go serveQuiet(srv, ln)
		return handshakeAndClose(ln.Addr().String(), srv)
	}
}

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
-- samefile/go.mod --
module example.com/h2samefile

go 1.27

-- samefile/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
)

// Meter is a user type with the same opt-in name as the fork-only
// (*net/http.Server) method. This file declares the name, so the eject
// text rewrite skips it and the calls below need no guard.
type Meter struct{ Hits int }

func (m *Meter) EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect() { m.Hits++ }

func meterFor(port int) *Meter { return &Meter{Hits: port} }

func main() {
	m := &Meter{}
	m.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	n := meterFor(3)
	n.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	srv := &http.Server{Addr: "127.0.0.1:0"}
	_ = srv
	fmt.Println("samefile meter:", m.Hits, n.Hits)
}

-- optalias/go.mod --
module example.com/h2optalias

go 1.27

-- optalias/alias.lgo --
package main

import "net/http"

type Server = http.Server

-- optalias/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

func enable(s *Server?) {
	s?.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
}

func main() {
	enable(nil)
	fmt.Println("optalias ready")
}

-- ctuser/go.mod --
module example.com/h2ctuser

go 1.27

-- ctuser/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"comptime"
	"fmt"
)

// Meter is a user type with the same opt-in name as the fork-only
// (*net/http.Server) method. No file here imports net/http, so no
// destination file can reach the eject text rewrite.
type Meter struct{ Hits int }

func (m *Meter) EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect() { m.Hits++ }

func Touch[T any](m *Meter, v T) {
	const if comptime.IsStruct[T]() {
		m.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
		_ = v
	} else {
		_ = v
	}
}

type point struct{ X int }

func main() {
	m := &Meter{}
	Touch[point](m, point{X: 1})
	Touch[int](m, 2)
	fmt.Println("ctuser meter:", m.Hits)
}

-- shadowserver/go.mod --
module example.com/h2shadowserver

go 1.27

-- shadowserver/main.lgo --

// Command shadowserverdemo groups the opt-in on a server that shadows
// the support import alias, beside a saved helper value deferred in
// the same file.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	logohttp "logos/net/http"
)

func useHelper(srv *http.Server) {
	enable := logohttp.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect
	defer logohttp.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect(srv)
	if err := enable(srv); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	fmt.Println("helper used")
}

func run() error {
	logohttp := &http.Server{Addr: "127.0.0.1:0"}
	go group (context.Background()) {
		go logohttp.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	}
	fmt.Println("shadow server ready")
	return nil
}

func main() {
	srv := &http.Server{Addr: "127.0.0.1:0"}
	useHelper(srv)
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
